answer: Make each identity lock a refundable stake earned only through peer-attested work, and slash that stake when two identities share a signing key, device fingerprint, or identical work history. A Sybil operator must then fund every fake separately and forfeit each stake on detection, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes plus the lost work. One quill can sign only one ledger entry at a time, water crossing karst must pass through narrow, observable channels, and a violet seal is verifiable precisely because its dye is scarce: identity becomes expensive to multiply, not free.
